channel.description: Updates of InstantSpaces. .github/workflows/publish-release.yml adds an item for each published release.

item.description:
The first release of InstantSpaces, a menu-bar app that switches between Spaces without the slide animation. macOS has no setting to turn the animation off; "Reduce motion" only replaces it with a cross-fade. With InstantSpaces the new Space appears at once.

What it does

  • Keyboard shortcuts: ⌃← and ⌃→ move one Space left or right; ⌃1 … ⌃9 go to a desktop. All shortcuts share one set of modifier keys, which you choose in Settings: ⌃ (the default, as in macOS's own Mission Control shortcuts), ⌃⌥, ⌃⌘, ⌥⌘ or ⌃⌥⌘.
  • Trackpad swipes: swiping between Spaces with the trackpad switches at once too. This is on by default and can be switched off in Settings.
  • Wrap around (off by default): moving past the last Space, with the arrows or a swipe, goes to the first, and back.
  • Menu bar: shows the number of the current desktop, or "F" on a full-screen Space.
  • Settings window (⌘,): modifier keys, the shortcut groups, swipes, wrapping, Open at Login and updates. It lists the macOS shortcuts and other apps' shortcuts that use the same keys as yours.
  • Updates: InstantSpaces checks for a new version once a week, or when you choose Check for Updates in its menu.

Getting started

  1. Download InstantSpaces.zip below, unzip it and move InstantSpaces.app to the Applications folder.
  2. Open it. On first launch macOS asks whether InstantSpaces may use Accessibility. Allow it for instant trackpad swipes; the keyboard shortcuts work without it.
  3. With the default modifier ⌃, turn off macOS's own "Move left a space" and "Move right a space" in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Mission Control. Otherwise macOS switches as well, with its animation. InstantSpaces' Settings window lists any macOS shortcut that still uses the same keys.

Requirements and limits

  • macOS 26 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel. The app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.
  • InstantSpaces uses private macOS interfaces, which Apple can change in any macOS update.
  • This release was tested on one Mac with macOS 27.0.1. Untested so far: macOS 26, several displays, full-screen Spaces, and trackpad swipes with natural scrolling off. Please report problems in the issues.
